approach: Add one prose const, CODE_CLAIMS_RULE, to crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs and append it to the Report section of planner_brief after FIELD_MEANING_RULE. The text requires each claim about existing behavior (what consumes a state, which sites produce each error or state class, which input forms an existing rule accepts, which records a gate reconciles, a role or config limit) to name the function and file:line the planner read. It requires a plan that classifies errors or states to list every producer site with its class. It tells a revising planner to settle each finding that names a file and function by reading that code and citing file:line, and to answer a finding about an unlisted adjacent path (max_concurrency path, role limits, records read from the branch) by listing that path in dependents. The Report section is shared by first-round and revision briefs, so one text serves both. A new test in briefs.rs checks the wording in both inputs. The existing Report size pin test (briefs.rs:3959) gets the new rule's length added to its bound. A CHANGELOG entry names the root cause. No refusal rule is added, frame.planner is untouched, and the data files and core crates are unchanged.

decisions.choice: Put the new text in the planner brief's Report as a separate const next to OPEN_QUESTION_RULE, REAL_RECORDS_RULE and FIELD_MEANING_RULE.
decisions.reason: The failing stage lacked this information in its brief. The Report is the one section both first-round and revision briefs share (planner.rs:146-149), so one text covers both. The sibling rules are separate consts that each have their own test, so this follows the pattern and keeps its own doc comment naming the root cause.

rejected.why: Out of scope. The brief says it has only 95 tokens of headroom, and the planner budget line in docs/system-facts.md would move.

rejected.option: A pre-critic admission check that refuses a plan with an unsupported claim or open question
rejected.why: Out of scope. Whether a claim is backed by the code cannot be judged without the repository, which is why the existing OPEN_QUESTION_RULE doc comment (planner.rs:62-63) keeps caller listing as prose. A refusal also adds a share of refused readings to measure.

The existing test planner_brief_tells_the_planner_to_settle_code_questions_by_reading (briefs.rs:1818-1832) pins its wording. A separate const keeps that test valid and lets the new test pin the new text alone.

files.purpose: Add a pub(super) const CODE_CLAIMS_RULE with a doc comment naming the root cause and jobs 20261030-013555-f5qm, 20261031-030119-tw3v, 20261103-075205-wbtm. Append {CODE_CLAIMS_RULE} after {FIELD_MEANING_RULE} in the Report format string of planner_brief (line 148).
Add a test for the new wording in a first-round and a revision brief. Update the Report size pin test (3938-3972) to include the new rule's length.
Add an entry under [Unreleased] ### Added naming the root cause, the const, the test commands and that no refusal rule was added.

steps: In crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs add `pub(super) const CODE_CLAIMS_RULE: &str = "...";` after FIELD_MEANING_RULE, with a doc comment naming the root cause (the brief asked to settle questions and list callers but never required each claim about existing behavior to cite the function and file:line read, nor revisions to settle code-named findings by reading) and the three jobs, and saying it is information, not a refusal. Text: each claim about existing behavior (what consumes a state, which sites produce each error or state class, which input forms an existing rule accepts, which records a gate reconciles, a role or config limit) names the function and file:line you read, and a plan that classifies errors or states lists every producer site (every bail!/Err site feeding the arm) with its class. On a revision, settle each finding that names a file and function by reading that code and citing file:line, not by assertion or by leaving it open; answer a finding about an unlisted adjacent path (for example the max_concurrency path, role limits, records read from the branch) by listing that path in dependents.
Append `\n\n{CODE_CLAIMS_RULE}` after `{FIELD_MEANING_RULE}` in the Report format string at planner.rs:148.

In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs add test planner_brief_requires_code_claims_to_cite_the_code_in_both_rounds near line 1832. It builds planner_inputs(None) and planner_inputs(Some(PlanRevision{previous: plan(1), findings: vec![finding(Severity::Major, FindingSource::Critic, "F")], resumed_from: None})). For each it takes the text after `## Report` and asserts the const appears exactly once, has no newline, and that the Report holds the needles `function and file:line`, `every producer`, `class`, `accepted`, `reconcile`, `settle each finding`, `dependents`, `max_concurrency`.

Update the_planner_brief_states_the_real_records_rule_once_within_its_bound (briefs.rs:3959) to add `+ super::planner::CODE_CLAIMS_RULE.len() + 2` to the bound, with a comment, and update the assert message format.

Add the CHANGELOG.md entry as the first bullet under ## [Unreleased] ### Added (line 22): root cause, failure class plan-leaves-code-answerable-questions-open-and-skips-adjacent-existing-path-fails-planning-rounds, the eight introspections' common cause, jobs 20261030-013555-f5qm, 20261031-030119-tw3v and 20261103-075205-wbtm (recorded no candidate; their work is not redone), the const and test names, the commands, that no refusal rule is added (0% refused) and the frame and token budgets are unchanged.
Run cargo fmt --all, then cargo test -p athena-context planner_brief and the full checks.

risks.risk: A longer Report may be skimmed by the planner, so the rule has little effect.
risks.mitigation: The text is short and generic, and it extends the existing OPEN_QUESTION_RULE without repeating its caller-listing sentence. The test checks that the const appears once and has no newline. Whether the planner follows it is not measured; the changelog says so.

risks.risk: The existing size pin fails on the longer Report and breaks the test check.
risks.mitigation: Update the size pin's bound in the same step and run cargo test -p athena-context planner_brief, which selects the pin test.

risks.risk: A revising planner reads the instruction to settle findings by reading as permission to skip the finding text.
risks.mitigation: The Report in the revision brief appears after the findings, so both appear in one brief. The wording tells the planner to settle each finding by reading, not to ignore it, and the existing line `Answer each in the new plan` stays.

risks.risk: The new text accidentally contains the string used to split the Report section in tests.
risks.mitigation: Use the quoted marker `## Report` as in the existing tests: split on `## Report` and take nth(1). The new const text must not contain the string `## Report`.

demonstrations.method: The new test checks the Report text for each content element. A read of planner.rs shows the const's doc comment names the root cause and the three job ids, and shows the const is appended after FIELD_MEANING_RULE in the Report.

demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The Report contains the needles for state consumers, error or state producers with class, accepted input forms, gate-reconciled records, role or config limits, and function plus file:line. The const doc comment names jobs 20261030-013555-f5qm, 20261031-030119-tw3v and 20261103-075205-wbtm.
